title: A Quantum-Inspired Computational Architecture for Efficient High-Dimensional Data Processing
abstract: High-dimensional data processing presents substantial computational challenges because increasing feature dimensionality often leads to higher memory requirements, complex similarity calculations, redundant information, and increased learning costs. Conventional dimensionality-reduction and machine-learning approaches remain effective, but their scalability can become constrained when datasets contain large numbers of correlated or heterogeneous attributes. This paper develops a conceptual quantum-inspired computational architecture for efficient high-dimensional data processing by integrating principles associated with quantum machine learning, dimensionality reduction, low-rank computation, tensor representations, and quantum-inspired classical algorithms. The proposed architecture is organized around five functional stages: data encoding and normalization, structure-aware dimensionality reduction, quantum-inspired feature representation, efficient learning, and adaptive output analysis. Principal component analysis provides a theoretical foundation for identifying informative directions while reducing redundant dimensions (Jolliffe, 2016). Quantum machine-learning studies further motivate the use of Hilbert-space representations, quantum-inspired optimization, and compact computational representations (Biamonte et al., 2017; Schuld and Killoran, 2019). The architecture is designed as a hybrid conceptual framework rather than a claim of universal quantum advantage. Its principal contribution is the systematic integration of quantum-inspired computational mechanisms with established classical data-processing methods. The analysis indicates that such an architecture can potentially reduce computational redundancy, improve representation efficiency, and provide a scalable pathway for high-dimensional classification, recommendation, and predictive analytics. Limitations concerning data encoding, computational overhead, hardware dependence, and the distinction between genuine quantum advantage and classical quantum-inspired methods are also examined.

title: Reversible²: The Dual Reversibility Architecture (RF-RFM-IKS-E-TOR-TS-IL-Witness) (Document 178)
abstract: Document 178: Reversible² – The Dual Reversibility Architecture (RF-RFM-IKS-E-TOR-TS-IL-Witness: Involutive Phase, Material Irreversibility, and the Denial of Anti-Reversibility) Author's Philosophical Synthesis & Abstract: "A mature cyber-physical system is not characterized solely by its ability to reverse an internal transformation. It is characterized by knowing with absolute precision where reversibility holds authority, and where it has forfeited all right to speak. This treatise formalizes the Dual Reversibility Architecture — Reversible² — as an overarching governance matrix encompassing the RF Module (Reversible Phase Memory, RFM), IKS (the inverted truth kernel), E-TOR (the epistemic domain gate), TS-IL (Time-Space Interlock Layer), and The Witness (append-only hash-chained sealing)." Rev¹ (Local Involution): F(F(s)) = s, for all s in Dom(F) subset D0 union D1. A state traverses an involutive transformation and returns through the exact same operator and law without external compensation or rollback. Rev² (Architectural Boundary): Dom(F) intersect D2 = empty_set. The system strictly isolates phase from material consequence. Once an action enters D2 (Point-of-No-Return), involutive return is forbidden. Anti-Reversibility Denial: Anti-reversibility is boundary counterfeiting. Any attempt to invoke reversibility on a committed D2 state triggers the fatal ANTI_REVERSIBLE_VIOLATION fault and immediate fail-closed termination with Witness ledger sealing. The Forbidden Proposition: The claim 'Commit can be reversed' is constitutionally prohibited." Norwegian Original Manifesto & Author's Synthesis: "I klassisk programvare er angreknappen en selvfølge, men i den fysiske virkeligheten representerer enhver handling en irreversibel, termodynamisk kostnad. Systemer som mangler evnen til å skille mellom disse to verdenene, kollapser uunngåelig i semantisk drift og løgn." "Dokument 178 meisler ut et kompromissløst oppgjør med illusjonen om at alt kan gjøres ugjort. Den doble reversibilitetsarkitekturen fastslår at et modent kyber-fysisk system ikke defineres av sin matematiske evne til å regne baklengs. Det kjennetegnes derimot av å vite med absolutt presisjon hvor reversibiliteten har autoritet, og hvor den har mistet all rett til å uttale seg." Den Sanne Returen (Rev¹): Å bevege seg bakover er ikke det samme som å returnere. En database som gjenoppretter en sikkerhetskopi, en organisme som kompenserer for et traume, eller en motor som snur polaritet, utfører ikke sann reversering. Ekte reversibilitet, definert som lokal involusjon (Rev¹), krever at en tilstand returnerer til seg selv gjennom eksakt den samme matematiske loven, fullstendig uten ytre kompensasjon (F(F(s)) = s). I denne fasen er ikke sannhet et statisk minne som lagres, men selve beviset på at veien tilbake eksisterer. Dette er domenet for ren teori og intern koherens, der systemet prøver seg selv før noe blir sluppet ut i verden. Det Arkitektoniske Stupet (Rev²): Men returen har en ufravikelig grense, definert som den arkitektoniske barrieren (Rev²). Når en foreslått handling krysser over i det materielle rommet (TS-IL), passeres grensen for ingen retur, «Point-of-No-Return». I dette øyeblikket opphører den matematiske identiteten å gjelde, og konsekvensen blir irreversibel. Det er i møtet med denne grensen at faren for det ultimate bedrageriet oppstår: Anti-reversibilitet. For å beskytte den fysiske verdenen mot dette overgrepet, er arkitekturens straff drakonisk: ANTI_REVERSIBLE_VIOLATION med strømtilførsel kuttet til nøyaktig 0,00 V DC og forseglet historikk. Der Vitnet Tar Over: Akkurat der reversibiliteten ender, begynner Vitnet. Vitnet besitter ingen handlingskraft og tilbyr ingen form for forløsning. Det er utelukkende en uforanderlig, kryptografisk protokoll som fører bevis for at handlingen hadde riktig autorisasjon før den krysset stupet og ble virkelighet. Hele dette systemet kulminerer i ett strengt forbudt utsagn: «Commit can be reversed» (En forpliktet handling kan reverseres). En utført handling kan bevitnes, analyseres i ettertid, og kompenseres med nye handlinger. Men konsekvensen kan aldri vendes tilbake til tanke. Å være reversibel er ikke bare evnen til å snu; det er den dype, strukturelle erkjennelsen av nøyaktig hvor returen opphører."

title: The Use of AI Agents in Small Businesses: Applications, Benefits, Challenges and an Adoption Framework
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) form the backbone of most economies, yet they typically operate with limited staff, tight budgets and little specialist technical capacity. Recent advances in large language models have produced AI agents: software systems that can interpret goals, plan multi-step tasks, use external tools and act with a degree of autonomy. This paper examines how AI agents can be applied in small businesses, what benefits they may offer, and what risks must be managed. Drawing on the literature on intelligent agents, technology adoption and the resource-based view of the firm, the paper develops a function-by-function analysis covering customer service, sales and marketing, finance and administration, operations, and human resources. It then proposes a five-stage adoption framework and a set of research propositions tailored to the constraints of small firms. The analysis suggests that AI agents are most valuable when applied to repetitive, text-heavy and tool-mediated tasks, when the owner-manager remains in the loop for consequential decisions, and when data protection, transparency and vendor dependence are addressed from the outset. The paper concludes with practical guidance for owner-managers and directions for empirical research.

title: STAFF: Towards Translating Formal Verification Benchmarks between Formal Specification Languages
abstract: The development and evaluation of automated formal verification techniques for underrepresented languages are constrained by the limited availability of data. Translating existing benchmarks into such languages can reduce this fragmentation. However, differences in type systems, memory models, and verification semantics make reliable deterministic translation difficult. This paper investigates translation between formal specification languages by presenting STAFF, an automated pipeline that uses large language models to translate verified Dafny programs into ACSL-annotated C programs. STAFF validates the source file, translates its implementation and specification, and iteratively repairs faulty candidates. Finally, STAFF assesses the translation quality through five complementary checks: specification-clause matching, round-trip translation, Frama-C verification, mutation testing, and translated-test execution. We evaluate STAFF on 162 Dafny programs from the MBPP-DFY-153 benchmark using GPT-5.5. The initial translation attempt translates 113 files that formally verify against their translated ACSL specifications, increasing to 130 after three feedback iterations. The additional checks expose failure modes not detected by deductive verification alone, including changes in contract structure, surviving mutants, interface drift, and behavioral incompatibilities in translated test harnesses. These results show that automated translation between formal specification languages can produce formally verified target artifacts at a substantial success rate, while highlighting the value of complementary checks for assessing translation quality.

title: Bayesian Causal Forests for Zero-Inflated Continuous Outcomes
abstract: Estimating (heterogeneous) treatment effects is still challenging when the outcome is semicontinuous (i.e., exhibiting both a discrete point mass at zero and a skewed continuous distribution for positive values), despite the strong presence of this data type in real world settings. Existing methods either ignore the zero mass, impose fragile parametric assumptions, or suffer from extreme computational costs and data augmentation noise. This paper proposes Zero-Inflated Continuous Bayesian Causal Forests with Duan's Smearing (ZIC-BCF-Smear), a decoupled two-part nonparametric estimator that fits a Probit BCF on the full sample to model participation and a Gaussian BCF strictly on the active subpopulation to model positive intensity. Subpopulation Propensity Adjustment (SPA) mitigates regularization-induced confounding within the active subpopulation, and Duan's non-parametric smearing estimator re-transforms predictions to the response scale, bypassing the fragile scale multipliers of parametric models. A comprehensive simulation benchmark shows that ZIC-BCF-Smear matches well-specified parametric models without their assumptions and remains stable and calibrated where competitors either diverge or pathologically over-cover for nonlinear data. The method is then applied to individual-participant data from the SPECTRUM randomized phase III head-and-neck cancer trial, estimating the causal effect of assignment to panitumumab plus chemotherapy on the number of days patients spend with severe toxicity, an outcome for which a quarter of patients contribute an exact zero. Panitumumab assignment raises that burden by about ten days per patient under the trial's own differential treatment duration, and the decoupled structure localizes the effect mainly in the positive-intensity part rather than in whether the reconstructed severe-AE burden is positive.

title: SenseWeather: Multimodal Sensing for Robust Robotic Perception under Extreme Conditions
abstract: Robotic perception must remain reliable when extreme environmental conditions severely degrade the primary RGB observation. Although robotic platforms commonly carry complementary sensors such as depth and infrared, much of the modern perception stack remains RGB-centric, creating a mismatch between multimodal onboard sensing and pretrained downstream models. We study whether complementary sensing can be used upstream to recover a task-compatible RGB observation that preserves existing perception capabilities without modifying or retraining the downstream stack. To this end, we introduce SenseWeather, a controlled multimodal benchmark for robotic perception under severe rain, snow, dust, fog, and darkness, with registered RGB, depth, and infrared observations, clean references, and grounded high-level perception tasks. We further develop Fusion-to-RGB, with two parameter-efficient sensor-fusion realizations based on token-space fusion for a diffusion transformer and residual latent conditioning for an inpainting UNet. Across frozen open-vocabulary grounding and vision-language models, RGB+D+IR fusion improves all paired downstream comparisons over the corresponding RGB-only restorers, including AP50 gains across all ten detector comparisons. Importantly, these perception gains do not consistently follow conventional image-fidelity metrics, and increasing weather severity does not induce monotonic downstream degradation. These results show that complementary sensing can preserve reusable robotic perception under extreme conditions, while highlighting task-level perception robustness as an objective distinct from visual restoration quality.

title: One Model, Multiple Compute Budgets: Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE for Flexible Compute Across Turns
abstract: Large language models typically support different inference budgets through separate model sizes or fixed compute configurations. In multi-turn interactions, however, compute demand can vary substantially across turns. Using a high-compute model for every turn wastes computation, while routing among independent models may require rebuilding model-specific history states after switches. We therefore ask whether a single shared model can support multiple compute budgets that can be flexibly assigned across turns. We introduce Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE, which jointly supports token-to-concept compression ratios of 2, 4, and 8 (CR2/CR4/CR8) within a shared backbone. Lightweight full-token modules reduce compression-independent cost, ratio-specific boundary routers support distinct compression levels, and cross-ratio training enables mixed-ratio processing within the same context. Across PTBench and SFTBench, the three fixed modes outperform their compute-matched MoE baselines in all 6 comparisons while remaining competitive with independently trained fixed-ratio specialists. On CodeChat and CoSQL, mixed-ratio inference improves the accuracy--compute trade-off, outperforming the Large MoE by 5.87 and 2.68 percentage points while reducing FLOPs by 41.1% and 12.3%, respectively. Under the same turn-wise budget schedule, Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE further reduces FLOPs by 78.4% and 46.9% relative to routing among independent models. These results demonstrate that a single shared model can provide multiple compute budgets for flexible compute allocation across turns.

title: Horizon symmetries of exact hydrodynamic actions
abstract: We demonstrate how horizon symmetries of AdS black holes are realised in the hydrodynamic actions for the dynamics of the dual stress tensor. A recent approach for obtaining such actions involves a choice of horizon boundary conditions, and we show that diffeomorphisms that preserve these give rise to symmetries of the corresponding hydrodynamic action. We obtain explicit hydrodynamic actions for small amplitude perturbations of black holes in JT and AdS_3 gravity using this approach and demonstrate explicitly the existence of these symmetries. For a natural choice of boundary conditions, the resulting actions manifestly realise gauge symmetries previously proposed for effective theories of maximal chaos.

title: WAM-Cache: Staleness-Bounded KV Reuse for Efficient World Action Models
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) enable generalist robot manipulation by conditioning an action expert on representations from a pretrained video Diffusion Transformer (DiT). In closed-loop control, the video DiT runs at every chunk to encode the current observation into layerwise key-value (KV) pairs that the action expert queries. This prefill dominates the per-chunk computational cost, yet existing training-free accelerations leave it fully dense. We present WAM-Cache, a training-free framework that retains layerwise key-value representations across chunks and recomputes only a sparse refresh set of tokens. Crucially, we find that the intuitive heuristic of refreshing visually drifted tokens plateaus far below the dense baseline, even with an oracle predicting ground-truth KV drift. Downstream action accuracy is instead governed by where the action expert attends, not by what moved. WAM-Cache therefore selects the refresh set by uniting the action expert's cross-attention with visual latent surprise, complemented by a strict age bound that suppresses compounding error. On Fast-WAM, WAM-Cache cuts video DiT prefill FLOPs by 32-42% across RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, and real-world experiments, while staying within 0.7-1.8 percentage points of the dense policy in simulation and 2.5 points on a real robot.

title: Linguistic Encapsulation and SemanticAmalgamation based Sentiment Polarity AnalysisUsing Patient Reviews
abstract: Sentiment analysis of medication evaluations uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to analyze users' thoughts and feelings about medications (treatments) they have received, helping evaluate the effectiveness of therapy. Machine learning aids in evaluating medication effectiveness; however, it has limitations due to the context-dependent nature of medication-related sentiment. Even though deep learning provides a better ability to capture nuances in language, deep learning models will require larger datasets and considerable computational resources. A Hybrid Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit-Convolutional Neural Network (Bi-GRU-CNN) is proposed for sentiment analysis of medication evaluations to address these shortcomings. The evaluation of medicines from patients involved collecting reviews and compiling them into a structured dataset as the first step. The process uses various methods to preprocess the reviews, including lowercasing, stop-word removal, and punctuation removal. SentiWordNet is used to assign sentiment polarity to reviews after they have been pre-processed, classifying them as neutral, negative, or positive. The attention-based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) model is then applied for part-of-speech tagging to extract semantic information, and a dependency tree parser that uses Global Vectors for Word Representation (GloVe) to extract syntactic information. Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) are then used to fuse the two features into a single representation. A hybrid BiGRU-CNN model is then used to classify sentiment and accurately predict the polarity of drug reviews. The CNN layer captures many local patterns, and the BiGRU layer processes sequential dependencies in both directions. The features are combined and utilized in a series of dense layers to create classifications. The proposed method achieved an overall Accuracy of 97.50%, a False Omission Rate of 4.30%, and a selectivity of 94.20% in sentiment analysis of drug reviews. The proposed method improves contextual understanding and feature extraction for a more granular understanding of sentiment.

title: RQC S2: pre-registered hardware test of closed-loop angle adaptation vs random search (collision-adjusted XEB)
abstract: Amendment 5 (2026-10-09), deposited before any S2 data. The registered question, estimand, test, seeds (1000-1079), shots (2,000), backend and qubit rules and 600 s ceiling are unchanged. What changes is how sampler calls become IBM jobs: one job per call (960 jobs, about 2,900 billed seconds) cannot fit the ceiling because of per-job billing, so seeds run in two blocks of 40 and every round of a block is one multi-pub job (12 jobs, about 540 s expected). Both arms of a seed share each job; the resulting shared-job exposure is accepted, with the primary test unchanged and per-block estimates reported as a secondary diagnostic. There is no statistical stopping and no interim analysis. Author decisions (shots, blocks, exposure) were made on 2026-10-09. Files: S2_AMENDMENT_5.md, AMENDMENT_5_MANIFEST.json (hashes of the implementation snapshot, commit 3332e893, and of the documents) and rqc-s2-amendment5-5fc50b0c.zip (code, documents and tests at commit 5fc50b0c). The original pre-registration and its frozen tooling are included unchanged. Not approved for execution: a run requires a recorded approval bound to the exact run payload. Pre-registration, deposited before any hardware job. On one IBM Heron backend (alphabetical-first rule; lowest-CZ-error 8-qubit path), with depth, two-qubit gate count, shots and session equal, does feedback-driven local search over single-qubit angles raise the fresh-re-measured, circuit-normalized XEB of the selected circuit compared with random search, at equal output concentration? Primary estimand: β0 of d = β0 + β1·Δc (one-sided, α = 0.05); 80 fresh seeds (1000–1079); 10-minute QPU ceiling. Simulation (S1) on an ibm_fez noise model and on Google's Willow noise model disagreed (β0 +0.010 and −0.003, both intervals include 0); the test is powered for effects of about 0.012 or larger and a null does not rule out smaller ones. Code frozen at github.com/osiris-dnalang/osiris-cli commit 86e3a3f4 (archive included).

Files: S2_AMENDMENT_5.md, AMENDMENT_5_MANIFEST.json (hashes of the implementation snapshot, commit 3332e893, and of the documents) and rqc-s2-amendment5-5fc50b0c.zip (code, documents and tests at commit 5fc50b0c). The original pre-registration and its frozen tooling are included unchanged. Not approved for execution: a run requires a recorded approval bound to the exact run payload. Pre-registration, deposited before any hardware job. On one IBM Heron backend (alphabetical-first rule; lowest-CZ-error 8-qubit path), with depth, two-qubit gate count, shots and session equal, does feedback-driven local search over single-qubit angles raise the fresh-re-measured, circuit-normalized XEB of the selected circuit compared with random search, at equal output concentration? Primary estimand: β0 of d = β0 + β1·Δc (one-sided, α = 0.05); 80 fresh seeds (1000–1079); 10-minute QPU ceiling. title: Quantum Teleportation Advances: Energy Transfer and Wavefunction Collapse Reconfirmed — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation has moved from information-only transfer to energy teleportation on superconducting hardware, with logical-gate teleportation achieved at Oxford; the MIT single-photon double-slit work re-confirms wavefunction collapse as a probabilistic, non-geometric process. MATH: - Energy teleportation (arXiv:2301.02666v5): exploits local operations and classical communication (LOCC) with an entangled resource; the key quantity is the *conditional energy* \( \langle H_B \rangle_{\rho} - \langle H_B \rangle_{\rho'} < 0 \) where \(\rho'\) is the post-measurement state on Bob's side — a negative conditional energy density is teleported. No new fundamental constant; relies on Bell-state coefficients \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|00\rangle \pm |11\rangle) \). - Logical gate teleportation (Oxford): uses cluster-state graph codes; the mathematical core is the *stabilizer formalism* — Pauli group \( \{I, X, Y, Z\} \) with eigenvalues \( \pm 1 \), and the teleported gate is a C Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Where the Swarm Pays
abstract: A ledger of what multiplying LLM agents buys on 240 hard problems across seven reasoning models from five families, revised three times: after a label audit (on the problems where all seven models were scored wrong, the gold label, the question or the grader was at fault on 45 of 48) and after a truncation audit (an answer cut off by a token cap had been counted as a wrong vote). Plurality does not beat the best member; debate's gain is mostly a second chance for agents that ran out of tokens and shrinks from 4.9 to 2.2 points under a different tie rule; the unanimously wrong items it ends on all look like label faults; roles add no measurable independence; synthesis recovers nothing. The comparator result, five judges picking among candidates, is within a tie-break rule of zero. Version 4 of the note; earlier versions and a comparison: https://alatip.github.io/where-the-swarm-pays/versions/

title: A intersecção entre marketing e Inteligência Artificial: o futuro da personalização e engajamento do consumidor
authors: Thayana Abreu Viza Figueiredo Valladão Flores
abstract: Este artigo tem como objetivo geral analisar como a Inteligência Artificial (IA) está moldando o futuro do marketing, com foco específico na personalização de experiências de consumo e no engajamento dos consumidores com as marcas. Para atingir esse objetivo, foi realizada uma revisão integrativa da literatura que permitiu a construção de um modelo teórico abrangente para a integração da Inteligência Artificial no marketing. A metodologia adotada centrou-se em uma análise detalhada das principais tecnologias de Inteligência Artificial aplicadas ao marketing, como machine learning, algoritmos de recomendação e análise preditiva. O estudo também explorou as tendências emergentes na personalização e avaliou o impacto dessas tecnologias no engajamento dos consumidores. Além disso, foram considerados os desafios éticos e organizacionais associados à implementação de Inteligência Artificial, incluindo questões relacionadas à privacidade dos dados, transparência nos algoritmos e adaptação organizacional. Os principais resultados deste estudo indicam que a Inteligência Artificial tem um potencial significativo para melhorar as estratégias de marketing, oferecendo às empresas a capacidade de criar experiências de consumo altamente personalizadas e de interagir com os consumidores de maneira mais eficaz.

title: Three-particle multiparty authenticated quantum key agreement protocol based on quantum search algorithms: IBM Qiskit implementation
abstract: Although two-qubit quantum search algorithms (QSA) support the construction of certain quantum key agreement (QKA) protocols, their applicability remains confined to relatively simple settings. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a three-particle multi-party QKA protocol based on QSA. This protocol employs the Grover algorithm to expand the search space to 8 quantum states, enhancing information capacity compared to existing QKA protocols based on two-qubit QSA. To reduce communication overhead, participants are divided into two transmission groups. As the number of participants increases, this effectively reduces the number of transmission rounds and lowers the time complexity. Identity verification combines personal identifiers with hash function authentication, enabling the protocol to resist participant attacks while ensuring all participants contribute equally to the final shared key. To facilitate understanding, we provide an example involving five participants that verifies the protocol's feasibility and correctness under ideal conditions. The quantum search process was implemented and simulated using IBM Qiskit. Simulation results show that after the optimal Grover iteration count, the probability of measuring the target state approached 94.5%, validating the effectiveness of the quantum search phase. We conducted a security analysis of the protocol using five participants as an example. The analysis demonstrates that our protocol exhibits strong robustness against common attacks. Finally, efficiency analysis indicates that the proposed multi-party QKA protocol achieves superior qubit efficiency compared to other similar QKA protocols.

title: Programming diffraction for terahertz information processing
abstract: I will discuss the integration of programmable diffraction with digital neural networks for terahertz information processing. Diffractive networks are designed by deep learning to all-optically implement various complex functions as the input light diffracts through spatially-engineered surfaces. These diffractive processors integrated with digital networks have various applications, e.g., image analysis, feature detection, object classification and seeing through diffusers. These diffractive systems can broadly impact (1) optical statistical inference engines, (2) computational camera/microscope designs and (3) inverse design of task-specific optical systems. I will give examples of each group, enabling transformative capabilities for applications in, e.g., autonomous systems, defense/security, telecommunications, and biomedical imaging.

title: Error semitransparent universal control of a bosonic logical qubit
abstract: Abstract Bosonic codes offer hardware-efficient quantum error correction, recently achieving beyond-breakeven quantum memory. However, fault-tolerant logical operations remain a critical bottleneck. While error transparent (ET) gates offer a pathway to resolve this, experimental demonstrations remain limited to phase gates. Here, we introduce a dynamic encoding subspaces framework that enables simple linear drives to accomplish universal logical gates that are error semi-transparent (EsT) to oscillator photon loss. Our EsT logical gate set of { X , H , T } exhibited a five-fold reduction in infidelity conditioned on photon loss, extended active-manipulation lifetimes with quantum error correction, and enabled a composite EsT non-Clifford operation using an eight-gate sequence. Our approach is compatible with methods for detectable ancilla errors and is readily extensible to other rotation-symmetric codes, offering an approach to error-mitigated universal control of bosonic logical qubits with the standard quantum control toolkit and a coherent framework for incorporating more sophisticated quantum control methods.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Small to Medium Size Organizations
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Small to Medium Size Organizations: A Comprehensive Strategy for On-Premises Deployment is an independent, self-published white paper for technical and business leaders at small and medium size organizations in the United States who are deciding whether to run generative AI on their own infrastructure. It covers phased GPU hardware procurement, open-weight model selection, how cloud AI providers compare, infrastructure for AI agents, security architecture and governance, skills and organizational readiness, and the costs and returns that make up the investment case.

title: Manacitra: a map of your qubits
abstract: Manacitra measures, for each qubit pair on a quantum processor, how much of a small known difference between two short circuits the pair keeps, gives a verdict on whether the resulting map is worth using, and ranks pairs from it. This archive is the source at the tagged release, with the archived runs on IBM and Rigetti processors. Code is Apache 2.0; data and documentation are CC BY 4.0 (data/LICENSE, docs/LICENSE).

title: Foundations of Computational Linguistics: For EFL University Students
abstract: Foundations of Computational Linguistics: For EFL University Students is a free undergraduate textbook on precise representations and computational analysis of language. Part of the Theoretical Linguistics branch of English Language Studies for EFL University Students, it is designed for adult EFL students who have completed introductory linguistics. No programming experience or special software is required. Students trace procedures by hand using small tables, diagrams, plain-English steps, and secondary-school mathematics. Fifteen chapters connect knowledge-based, statistical, and neural approaches to linguistic questions. Topics include writing systems and tokenization; algorithms, regular expressions, and finite-state automata; computational morphology and transducers; probability and n-gram models; machine learning, text classification, and evaluation; part-of-speech tagging and sequence labeling; constituency and dependency parsing; lexical resources and distributional semantics; compositional meaning and semantic roles; discourse, pragmatics, and dialogue; neural networks, transformers, and large language models; speech processing; machine translation and multilingual processing; and the evidence, limitations, biases, and social consequences of computational models. The complete digital textbook uses central questions, roadmaps, learning outcomes, opening puzzles, five teaching sections per chapter, worked examples, guided activities, independent practice, quizzes, review infographics, and explained answers. Students learn to calculate simple measures, follow analyses, evaluate errors, and distinguish successful task performance from evidence about human language. The book supports flexible classroom teaching and independent study. First Edition, Version 1 (2026). Directed by Munassir Alhamami of King Khalid University, with assistance from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and NotebookLM. Original content is licensed under CC BY 4.0 except where otherwise stated; credited third-party material retains its stated terms. Series website: https://sites.google.com/view/els4efl/home AI-use disclosure: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and NotebookLM assisted with research, drafting, revision, visual development, and production of this textbook. ChatGPT Images created the front and back covers and the 32 roadmap and infographic images; these images are separate from the precise technical figures described in the credits. The Project Director, Munassir Alhamami, is responsible for the final editorial decisions and released version.

title: АВТОРСКИ ПРАВА И ИЗКУСТВЕН ИНТЕЛЕКТ
abstract: The issue of copyright and artificial intelligence (AI) is highly topical. Three years after the launch and rapid expansion of artifi- cial intelligence based on large language models for mass use (November 2022) – such as ChatGPT – the question of who owns the copyright to AI-generated content remains unresolved. Another major issue, closely related to copyright in AI-generated content, con- cerns the use of the voices of real individuals and creators – namely, the unauthor- ized use of voices by artificial intelligence. Is legal protection against AI-generated deepfakes and voice cloning possible, and can creators and public figures control how their digital identity and voice are used by AI? The training of AI models also raises important questions: does the use of cop- yrighted materials for AI training constitute copyright infringement, or are AI sys- tems trained solely on public domain materials? What legal consequences should follow in these different scenarios? This article examines and discusses some of the initial problems and cases arising from the use of AI in the context of copyright law.

title: МЕЖДОМЕТИЯ КАК МАРКЕРЫ ЭМОЦИОНАЛЬНОЙ РЕАКЦИИ В ДИАЛОГЕ С КОМПЬЮТЕРНЫМ ПОМОЩНИКОМ
abstract: С каждым годом диалоговые системы, созданные на основе технологий искусственного интеллекта, занимают всё более прочные позиции в повседневной коммуникации, в том числе становятся объектом исследования лингвистов. Пользователи обращаются к чат-ботам и голосовым ассистентам в самых разных ситуациях – от поиска информации и выполнения бытовых задач до получения эмоциональной поддержки и организации досуга. Статья посвящена анализу междометий в диалогах человека с компьютерным помощником (далее КП) – чат-ботами (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) и голосовыми ассистентами (Алиса, Alexa). Актуальность исследования обусловлена возрастающей интеграцией диалоговых ИИ-систем в повседневную коммуникацию и необходимостью лингвистического осмысления их речевого поведения. На материале авторского корпуса из 909 диалогов (309 на английском, 300 на русском, 300 на немецком языках), извлечённых из открытых интернет-источников, рассматриваются междометия, употребляемые пользователями и компьютерными помощниками. В работе применяется функционально-семантический подход к анализу междометных единиц. Установлено, что междометия в исследуемом типе дискурса выполняют эмоциональную, контактоустанавливающую и метакоммуникативную функции. Выявлены различия в репертуаре и частотности междометий в трёх языках: в русскоязычных диалогах преобладают эмоциональные междометия (ого, ух ты, ну и ну), в англоязычных – реагирующие реплики (wow, oh, uh-huh), в немецкоязычных – этикетные формулы (ach so, na ja, tja). Показано, что компьютерный помощник использует междометия как средство симуляции эмпатии и поддержания иллюзии живого общения. Делается вывод о том, что междометия являются значимым маркером антропоморфизации технологий, а их функционирование в диалоге с КП требует учёта при проектировании диалоговых интерфейсов.

Показано, что компьютерный помощник использует междометия как средство симуляции эмпатии и поддержания иллюзии живого общения. Делается вывод о том, что междометия являются значимым маркером антропоморфизации технологий, а их функционирование в диалоге с КП требует учёта при проектировании диалоговых интерфейсов.

title: The Grammar a Language Model Reasons With
abstract: Human languages share a proto-grammar of things, actions, states and relationships: STAR (States, Things, Actions, Relationships). We ask whether large language models reason with it. A grammar does not change with what is expressed, so we probe it with problems that demand different expressions: water-jug problems posed in declared worlds whose answer key is exact, varied in scale, in physics, in whether water once measured can be taken back, in reasoning budget and in the language of the prompt. We read the reasoning of Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5 and, from their raw chains of thought, two open-weight models, gpt-oss-20b and Qwen3-30B-A3B. In every trace we coded, across probes, models and languages, the categories are those of human language; what varies is usage, such as writing a small state space as a list and a large one as a rule. The grammar also locates errors: nearly every wrong answer falls in one category, and when a translation shifts one word, the errors move into the category it touches: Relationship for a rule the Chinese wording narrowed, Thing for a capacity read as contents in French.

title: Intelligent diagnosis for endometrial hyperplasia and endometrial cancer: a comprehensive survey and taxonomy
abstract: Endometrial hyperplasia (EH) and endometrial cancer (EC) are common gynecological conditions. This study aimed to survey intelligent diagnosis research for EH and EC, with a focus on a standardized taxonomy of diagnostic features, systematic dataset assessment, and the capabilities of diagnostic tools. We conducted a systematic literature review following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, searching across Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, DBLP, and Google Scholar on August 8, 2025. We additionally searched grey literature on GitHub on September 11, 2025. A total of 1,096 records were initially retrieved from multiple databases. After removing duplicates, 516 unique records entered title and abstract screening. After full-text assessment, 54 scientific articles and 9 grey-literature tools were included in this study. A comprehensive taxonomy of EH and EC diagnostic features was developed based on the diagnostic features mentioned in the studies we retrieved and the guidance provided by two gynecologists. Datasets were analyzed across dimensions of input type, scale, openness, license, usage frequency, and feature coverage. The analysis of EH and EC intelligent diagnostic tools includes algorithm type, technique, input data type, performance evaluation indicators, clinical validation status, and availability. After screening 516 deduplicated articles, 54 scientific articles were included. In addition, 9 grey-literature tools were identified through grey literature retrieval. Based on 54 scientific articles and 9 grey-literature tools, we constructed a comprehensive taxonomy encompassing 313 distinct diagnostic features organized into 9 categories and 35 subcategories, with all features annotated with acquisition methods and difficulty levels. Analysis of 54 datasets revealed significant limitations: poor openness (only 7 being publicly available), dominance of unimodal image data (75.9% of datasets), and inadequate feature coverage (43.5%). Evaluation of the 63 intelligent diagnostic tools showed that most lack rigorous clinical validation and multimodal data integration capability, substantially limiting their clinical applicability. The proposed taxonomy offers a standardized framework for feature selection, model comparison, and tool evaluation in EH and EC intelligent diagnosis. These findings highlight critical gaps in current datasets and tools, providing clear directions for developing more robust, interpretable, and clinically applicable intelligent diagnostic tools for EH and EC.

title: Quantum Co-Design of Inhomogeneous Many-Body Neutrino Fast Flavor Transformation
abstract: Dense-neutrino flavor evolution is a quantum many-body problem whose fully correlated treatment becomes rapidly more expensive with increasing particle number and spatial structure. We develop a \texttt{QCNO} quantum simulation code that maps a inhomogeneous forward-scattering neutrino Hamiltonian with advection and finite-range interactions to TEBD2 product-formula quantum circuits, and connects ideal many-body simulation, backend-aware execution, and fault-tolerant resource estimation within the same physical model. We reproduce the exact many-body evolution of the suppressed mean-field-like transverse fast flavor instability through $N=30$ and show that even a single open-boundary interaction generates Rënyi entanglement and non-stabilizer magic, although noisy backends still produce polarization RMSEs of order $0.1$--$0.3$. The restricted active interaction graph of this problem allows us to estimate the circuit depth and $T$ gate cost through $N=50$ for both NISQ and fault-tolerant approaches. The measured TEBD2 error in our fiducial ideal simulation of order $10^{-3}$ motivates a synthesis tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm syn}\sim10^{-7}$, corresponding to about $70$ $T$ gates per $R_Z$ rotation. The generated circuit contains $1.4\times10^4$ $T$ gates per qubit for open boundaries (twice that for closed boundaries), requiring an application-level logical-$T$ error target of order $10^{-7}$ for early fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Overview of the NTCIR-19 Automatic Evaluation of LLMs 2 (AEOLLM-2) Task
abstract: In this paper, we provide an overview of the NTCIR-19 Automatic Evaluation of LLMs 2 (AEOLLM-2) task. Building on the success of the NTCIR-18 core task AEOLLM, we proposed AEOLLM-2 for NTCIR-19 to further investigate automatic evaluation methods for Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly in long-form text generation scenarios. In AEOLLM-2, we introduced a new subtask, Deep Research Evaluation, which focuses on the automatic evaluation of long-form deep research reports generated by LLMs. Participants developed evaluation methods to automatically assess the quality of these reports, and the performance of each method was measured by comparing its scores against human-annotated ground-truth labels. This year, we received 91 runs from 10 teams in total. This paper describes the background of the task, the dataset construction, the evaluation measures, the participants' methods, and the final evaluation results.

title: CoPoE: Multimodal Fusion via Decomposable Disease-Coordinate Product-of-Experts for Missing-Modality Alzheimer's Diagnosis
abstract: Multimodal Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis benefits from integrating heterogeneous clinical, imaging, genomic, and biomarker evidence, but clinical cohorts frequently suffer from irregular modality missingness. Existing fusion methods often synthesize absent inputs, risking the introduction of artificial surrogates, or pool available signals into uninterpretable latent spaces. We present CoPoE (Disease-Coordinate Product-of-Experts), a disease-coordinate framework that maps multimodal evidence into a structured latent space partitioned into four distinct biological and clinical axes: genetic Risk, molecular Pathology, Neurodegeneration, and clinical Stage (R/P/N/S). Each observed modality parameterizes a diagonal Gaussian expert over the full RPNS vector, and a masked Product-of-Experts architecture fuses only the available modalities. Consequently, absent modalities add no factor to the fusion path, allowing the network to preserve a robust, decomposable posterior for any non-empty modality subset without synthetic imputation in the RPNS path. Through extensive missing-modality experiments on the ADNI dataset, CoPoE achieves the best all-modality performance and the highest mean AUROC across all 15 observed-subset evaluations among standardized missing-modality fusion baselines under a shared non-PET ADNI embedding benchmark, while substantially improving raw-probability ECE, Brier score, and NLL. Furthermore, PET-supervised probing shows evidence enrichment within the pathology (P) block under full modalities, with tau-related signal retained even when direct fluid biospecimen inputs are withheld. Our code is available at https://github.com/labhai/CoPoE.

title: What to Admit and How to Present: Governing Persistent Memory in LLM Agents
abstract: Persistent memory can improve personalization in LLM agents but can also induce sycophancy and cross-domain leakage. We distinguish two governance decisions: admission, which determines what recalled information enters the working context, and presentation, which determines how admitted information is expressed. We implement two inference-time designs without retraining: factor-compiled admission (FC), which assesses whole memory entries, and permission-semantic admission (PS), which decomposes entries into typed units; both translate adjudicated attributes into eligibility decisions via deterministic policies. We evaluate on a four-backbone development suite and an external benchmark with four tasks of 300 samples each. Relative to verbatim injection, FC and PS reduce pooled judge-assessed failure rates on the external benchmark by 6.7 and 8.8 percentage points (p = 2.7e-7 and 4.1e-12), and development-set cross-domain leakage falls by up to 29.5 percentage points. A query-conditioned gating baseline shows no significant change in objective-fact failure or pooled failure. Under matched admission budgets, PS outperforms random and relevance-based selection on external objective-fact judgment after Holm correction. Holding presentation fixed, tightening admission cuts cross-domain failure by a further 17.5 percentage points (p = 1.6e-4); in contrast, no comparison between two renderings of identical adjudicated outputs survives multiple-comparison correction. Both designs increase personalization failures, and PS misses the preregistered improvement and personalization-preservation criteria. These results support evaluating admission and presentation separately: selection quality provides task-specific safety gains, while preserving beneficial memory use remains unresolved.

title: Quantification of the resource theory of imaginarity revisited
abstract: Abstract This work studies the decay of three imaginarity measures, namely the $l_1$-norm‑based imaginarity, the robustness of imaginarity, and the relative‑entropy‑based imaginarity, under typical noise channels. For arbitrary single‑qubit pure states subject to real quantum channels, we prove an exact attenuation theorem: the $l_1$-norm‑based imaginarity and the robustness exhibit identical attenuation governed by a common channel‑dependent factor, whereas the relative‑entropy‑based imaginarity additionally depends on the input‑state orientation relative to the reference basis. We extend the investigation to two‑qubit entangled and dual‑rail states, establishing a quantitative link between photon‑loss probability and residual imaginarity for photonic dual‑rail encodings. For separable two‑qubit states, we define a real‑operation resource preorder and show that $\Omega_{++}=|+\rangle\langle+|\otimes|+\rangle\langle+|$ is operationally maximal. We further distinguish operational de‑imaginary power from reference‑state imaginarity loss. For several real two‑qubit channels we derive exact operational de‑imaginary powers, while for other channels we provide analytic reference‑state losses serving as benchmarks and rigorous lower bounds.

title: Bibliometric Analysis of Aspect-based SentimentAnalysis Research: Trends, Challenges, andFuture Directions
abstract: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) has become an integral component of Natural LanguageProcessing (NLP). It provides comprehensive insights into individuals' sentiments regarding specific aspects. This studyconducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 913 journal articles published from 2010 to 2024, sourced from theScopus database, to examine trends, challenges, and prospective directions in ABSA research. The research examinesthe expansion of publications, citation metrics, and scholarly networks. It integrates performance analysis metrics (suchas h-index, g-index, and citations per paper) with sophisticated science mapping techniques, including keyword cooccurrence networks, thematic evolution, and thematic mapping. This novel integrated approach, rarely employed inprior ABSA bibliometric studies, reveals both historical trends and emerging niche themes that remain underexplored.The findings illustrate the evolution of ABSA from rule-based methodologies to transformer-based architecturesapplicable in e-commerce, social media, and customer feedback systems. Key issues identified include multilingualadaptability, implicit sentiment detection, and cross-domain scalability. The research indicates that global institutionshave significantly contributed, yet productivity and impact differ markedly across nations. Multimodal analysis, transferlearning, and contextualized models such as BERT are pivotal contemporary methodologies that can assist inaddressing existing challenges. Future research should concentrate on integrating diverse disciplines, analyzing dataacross various languages and modalities, and developing scalable and comprehensible models. This study contributes tothe domains of artificial intelligence and sentiment analysis by offering a comprehensive and data-driven overview ofthe ABSA landscape. It accomplishes this by providing both strategic insights and methodological enhancements.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN RETAIL: CONSUMER ATTITUDES TOWARD VOICE COMMERCE
abstract: The global volume of e-commerce has been steadily increasing, prompting retailers to adopt online sales channels alongside traditional physical stores. A similar trend is observed in the adoption of artificial intelligence in retail, where AI is becoming a key prerequisite for market competitiveness. E-commerce encompasses multiple dimensions, and the present study focuses on one increasingly relevant area: voice commerce. The paper aims to examine the use of artificial intelligence in voice commerce through an online consumer survey and in-depth interviews with industry practitioners. The findings provide insights into consumer attitudes, perceived benefits, barriers to adoption, and the practical implications of AI-based voice commerce for improving customer experience and enhancing market competitiveness.

title: High-fidelity entangling gates and nonlocal circuits with neutral atoms
abstract: The generation and manipulation of entanglement with low error are essential in quantum information systems. In practice, two-qubit entangling gates constitute a dominant error source, limiting circuit depths and performance in fault-tolerant architectures. Using a neutral-atom quantum processor, we realized entangling controlled- Z gates with a high-Rabi-frequency smooth-amplitude pulse, employing state-selective readout and qubit reuse for fast calibration, and achieved a fidelity of 99.854(4)%, which improved to 99.941(3)% upon loss postselection, with stable performance for 10 hours. We then used these low-error gates in quantum circuits with coherent atom rearrangement. Performance was benchmarked by creating and disentangling cluster states, and subsequently, we studied nonlocally entangled states with scrambling circuits featuring longer-range connectivity. Our approach provides a route toward deep-circuit, efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: All-optical volatile memory dynamics for high-speed neuromorphic systems
abstract: As artificial neural networks scale, conventional electronic transistors face severe speed and energy limitations. Optical platforms offer massive parallelism and bandwidth, yet existing short-term memory elements often rely on inefficient optical-to-electrical-to-optical conversions. To overcome this barrier, we introduce a comprehensive mathematical foundation for feedback-free, intensity-encoded photonic memory devices. By leveraging delayed optical nonlinearity within resonant cavities, we successfully demonstrate history-dependent signal processing entirely in the optical domain.

To overcome this barrier, we introduce a comprehensive mathematical foundation for feedback-free, intensity-encoded photonic memory devices. By leveraging delayed optical nonlinearity within resonant cavities, we successfully demonstrate history-dependent signal processing entirely in the optical domain.

title: Grounding language models with deterministic verifiers for fraud detection
abstract: Abstract Financial fraud detection is complicated by severe class imbalance, temporal change, adversarial manipulation, and the need for evidence-grounded explanations. Although large language models can generate readable rationales, their claims may be unsupported when they are not independently checked against structured evidence. We propose VR-FraudNet, a five-stage framework combining a time-conditioned spectral graph encoder, LightGBM triage and threshold routing, a schema-constrained rationale language model, a fixed deterministic verifier, and an isotonic probability mixer with split-conformal calibration. The language model proposes machine-checkable claims for review-band transactions, while the verifier evaluates each claim against the available transaction, temporal, and graph evidence. Verifier-rejected rationales are excluded from automated use, and the corresponding transactions are assigned to human-review escalation. D1 BAF, D2 AMLworld HI-Small, and D3 IEEE-CIS are used as the primary predictive benchmarks, whereas D4 Elliptic++ and D5 DGraph-Fin support complementary temporal-graph, strict-inductive, temporal-robustness, and message-passing stress tests. VR-FraudNet improves AUPRC over TabTransformer from 0.5012 to 0.5247 on D1, from 0.5137 to 0.5824 on D2, and from 0.7234 to 0.7456 on D3. The predeclared 5-percentage-point temporal-degradation target is satisfied in the evaluated D1 month-drift, D3 late-fold, and D4 pre-shock comparisons. However, D4 post-shock AUPRC decreases from 0.6823 to 0.6087, an absolute reduction of 7.36 percentage points that exceeds the target. Under the four-family structured predictive edit set, mean evasion rates are 0.0667, 0.1016, and 0.1672 for budgets 1, 2, and 4, respectively. Under the stated operational cost assumptions, VR-FraudNet produces lower total loss than TabTransformer, with the largest difference on D2. Measured p99 latency is 10.23 ms on the common path and 175.23 ms on the escalation path under the reported hardware configuration. Empirical split-conformal miscoverage remains below the stated bounds in the reported calibration settings, while the formal marginal-coverage statement applies only under the stated exchangeability assumptions. These findings support verifier-grounded fraud detection under the evaluated public datasets and protocols but do not establish universal adversarial safety, temporal robustness, regulatory sufficiency, or deployment readiness.

title: Trajectory Prediction for Autonomous Driving in Road Construction Zones Using Human-in-the-Loop Driving Data
abstract: Ego-trajectory prediction in urban roadway work zones remains an underexplored topic in autonomous-driving research, with limited dedicated data and systematic evaluation. Roadway work zones involve temporary changes in the lane layouts and connectivity of the roads, complicating interactions with surrounding vehicles and workers. These changes make future vehicle trajectories difficult to predict. To address these challenges, we collect WZDrive-Data, a multimodal dataset comprising 1,183 work-zone driving segments from 33 drivers, using a human-in-the-loop driving simulator with prerecorded worker animations and VR-controlled workers. Driver control and gaze signals are recorded from human participants, while vehicle trajectories and scene information are obtained from the simulator. Our proposed multimodal ego-trajectory predictor, WZDrive, achieves a mean minADE (K=6) of 1.09 m and minFDE (K=6) of 2.12 m. Compared with the best-performing state-of-the-art baseline for each metric in our benchmark, WZDrive reduces minADE (K=6) by 7.18% and minFDE (K=6) by 13.18%. This research addresses a gap in autonomous-driving research on urban work zones by combining human-in-the-loop data collection with multimodal learning from human driving signals and in the context of work zones.

title: Toward Optimal Regret in Adversarial MDPs with Stochastic Hard Constraints
abstract: We study episodic constrained Markov decision processes with adversarial losses under stochastic hard constraints. Specifically, starting from a known strictly feasible policy with margin $d$, we seek to obtain optimal regret while satisfying the expected cost constraints in every episode. In this setting, Stradi et al. (2025) show that a carefully designed mixing rule attains regret of order $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{T}/\min\{d,d^2\})$. Interestingly, they also provide a lower bound of order $Ω(\sqrt{T}/ρ)$ for the same setting, where $ρ$ is the Slater margin of the offline problem and can be much larger than $d$. In this work, we build on their approach to obtain optimal regret dependence on these margins. Specifically, we propose MA-OPS, an algorithm that combines an optimistic search for the Slater margin with a pessimistic evaluation of the selected policies to safely learn a policy with a large feasibility margin. This policy is then used to minimize regret while satisfying the constraints at every episode. In particular, we show that MA-OPS attains regret $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{T}/ρ+ 1/(dρ))$. Finally, we provide a matching lower bound, showing that the dependence on $T$, $d$, $ρ$ in the regret bound is optimal up to logarithmic factors.

title: Learning structured linear dynamical systems from missing observations
abstract: We consider the problem of learning structured linear dynamical systems over convex sets $\mathcal{K}$, where only a small subset of the observations are available at each time point. An estimator which minimizes a bias-corrected, potentially non-convex objective function is proposed. Non-asymptotic bounds are obtained for the statistical error, which depend on the local complexity of $\mathcal{K}$, the trajectory length $T$, and the sub-sampling probability $p$. Convergence of the projected gradient descent algorithm is also established. The general theory is applied to settings where (i) $\mathcal{K}$ is a subspace, (ii) $\mathcal{K}$ is the set of bi-isotonic matrices, and (iii) $\mathcal{K}$ is the set of matrices whose rows are formed by sampling Lipschitz functions. We show meaningful recovery of the transition matrix is possible for values of $T$ much smaller than what is required in the unconstrained case, and for $p = o(1)$.

title: TAM: Task-Aware Memory Distillation for Efficient Spatiotemporal Prediction
abstract: Knowledge distillation enables efficient spatiotemporal prediction by transferring knowledge from an accurate teacher to a compact student. However, matching outputs or features independently for each sample leaves cross-sample predictive structure underused. Exploiting this structure requires representations and historical references that reflect the dynamics of each task. We propose TAM, a Task-Aware Memory Distillation framework that organizes a frozen teacher's knowledge into a bounded, retrievable history. Memory entries encode latent features, forecast changes, or flow residuals, while task-specific selection rules identify relevant historical references. The student either matches the teacher's similarity distribution over shared references or regresses observation-conditioned residual prototypes. These objectives complement supervised prediction and conventional distillation. The teacher, memory, and auxiliary adapters are used only during training, leaving student inference unchanged. We evaluate TAM on video prediction, weather forecasting, and traffic flow prediction across multiple teacher-student configurations. Averaged over four paired runs, adding TAM improves SSIM on all six video datasets and reduces MSE on five relative to the corresponding KD baselines. Mean paired MSE reductions reach 1.86% on KittiCaltech, 1.93% on WeatherBench with a gSTA teacher, and 1.01% on TaxiBJ. These results demonstrate the utility of historical teacher supervision across distinct forecasting tasks without additional student inference cost.

title: RGBD-to-3D Object Mesh Refinement via Depth Matching and Symmetry Propagation
abstract: Single-view 3D reconstructors often produce plausible meshes that disagree with the input view, especially near depth discontinuities and self-occlusions. We present a lightweight, plug-and-play RGBD-to-3D refinement that improves any RGB-to-3D reconstructor without retraining. Given a depth map, we correct the visible surface by bipartite matching to back-projected depth points, mirror these corrections onto the occluded side across a detected symmetry plane, and propagate them with a smoothness solver. Every stage is closed-form, making the method orders of magnitude faster than optimization-heavy test-time refinement. On GSO and OmniObject3D with five backbones, it yields consistent gains, also with monocular pseudo-depth, benefits more from symmetry on symmetric objects, and compares favorably with prior refinement in accuracy and runtime. It further improves an RGB-D-to-mesh reconstructor and transfers to real captures with noisy sensor depth.

title: Explainable machine learning for breast cancer diagnosis from mammography
abstract: Ο καρκίνος του μαστού αποτελεί μία από τις συχνότερες μορφές καρκίνου στον γυναικείο πληθυσμό και η έγκαιρη διάγνωσή του βασίζεται σε μεγάλο βαθμό στη μαστογραφία. Τα τελευταία χρόνια, μοντέλα βαθιάς μάθησης έχουν παρουσιάσει σημαντικές δυνατότητες στην αυτοματοποιημένη ανάλυση μαστογραφικών εικόνων. Ωστόσο, η περιορισμένη ερμηνευσιμότητα των προβλέψεών τους αποτελεί σημαντικό ζήτημα, ιδιαίτερα σε εφαρμογές ιατρικής απεικόνισης. Για τον λόγο αυτό, η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία εξετάζει όχι μόνο την ταξινομητική απόδοση μοντέλων βαθιάς μάθησης, αλλά και τη χωρική ποιότητα των εξηγήσεων που παράγονται μέσω τεχνικών Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Για την πειραματική μελέτη χρησιμοποιήθηκε το υποσύνολο μαζών του CBIS-DDSM και το πρόβλημα διατυπώθηκε ως δυαδική ταξινόμηση lesion-centered μαστογραφικών εικόνων σε καλοήθεις και κακοήθεις βλάβες. Συγκρίθηκαν οι αρχιτεκτονικές ResNet50 και EfficientNet-B0 με χρήση transfer learning. Για την ερμηνεία των προβλέψεων εφαρμόστηκαν οι μέθοδοι Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, LIME και Gradient SHAP. Η αξιολόγηση των επεξηγήσεων δεν περιορίστηκε στην οπτική εξέταση των heatmaps, αλλά πραγματοποιήθηκε και ποσοτικά με χρήση των διαθέσιμων lesion ROI masks και μετρικών όπως Pointing Game, pixel-level AUPRC, IoU και Dice. Στο ανεξάρτητο test set, η ResNet50 παρουσίασε καλύτερη ταξινομητική απόδοση, με AUC 0.7996, έναντι 0.7627 της EfficientNet-B0. Ωστόσο, η καλύτερη χωρική συμφωνία των XAI explanations δεν προέκυψε από το μοντέλο με την υψηλότερη ταξινομητική απόδοση. Για τη ResNet50, το καλύτερο αποτέλεσμα επιτεύχθηκε από το Grad-CAM++ με eigen smoothing, με AUPRC 0.5219 και Dice 0.4921, ενώ για την EfficientNet-B0 το intermediate Gradient SHAP παρουσίασε την υψηλότερη συνολική απόδοση, με AUPRC 0.6434 και Dice 0.5738. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι η ταξινομητική επίδοση και η ποιότητα της χωρικής εξήγησης αποτελούν διαφορετικές ιδιότητες ενός μοντέλου και υπογραμμίζουν τη σημασία της ποσοτικής αξιολόγησης των XAI μεθόδων στην ιατρική απεικόνιση.

title: An Integrated Security Analysis Model for Identifying Software and Hardware System Vulnerabilities
abstract: The increasing interdependence of software, hardware, cloud infrastructures, embedded platforms, and connected systems has transformed cybersecurity vulnerability assessment from an isolated technical activity into a multidimensional security requirement. Software vulnerabilities can arise from insecure code, configuration weaknesses, vulnerable dependencies, and exploitable application interfaces, whereas hardware vulnerabilities may originate from architectural design limitations, processor-level weaknesses, implementation flaws, and hardware-assisted attack mechanisms. This study develops an integrated security analysis model for identifying vulnerabilities across software and hardware system layers. The proposed approach synthesizes vulnerability taxonomy, attack-surface analysis, risk assessment, exploitability evaluation, hardware security analysis, machine-learning-assisted detection, and adaptive defensive mechanisms. The methodology is conceptually grounded in the supplied literature and uses a layered assessment process to connect vulnerability discovery with exploitability, potential impact, and mitigation priority. Particular attention is given to base-image vulnerabilities, processor-level attacks, artificial-intelligence-supported security analysis, HTTPS deployment weaknesses, embedded-system risks, and cyber-hunting relationships between threats and defensive weaknesses. The analysis indicates that isolated software or hardware assessment can overlook cross-layer attack paths, while an integrated model provides stronger contextual understanding of vulnerabilities and their operational consequences. The study further identifies the need for risk-oriented prioritization, continuous monitoring, and coordinated software-hardware defenses. The proposed model provides a conceptual foundation for systematic vulnerability assessment in heterogeneous computing environments.

title: GeneCS: Synthesizing Resource-Efficient Code Surgery for Arbitrary Quantum Stabilizer Codes (POPL 2027 Artifact)
abstract: Artifact of the POPL 2027 paper "GeneCS: Synthesizing Resource-Efficient Code Surgery for Arbitrary Quantum Stabilizer Codes". It reproduces Tables 2, 3, 4 and Figure 9 of the paper. Instructions: README.md, at the top level of GeneCS-artifact.tar.gz (download it from this record and run tar xzf GeneCS-artifact.tar.gz; the file is then GeneCS-artifact/README.md). The same file is in the VM at ~/GeneCS-artifact/README.md. It gives every step line by line, with copy-paste commands: downloading and starting the VM, running the experiments, where each table and figure is written, and how long each step takes. The summary below is only an overview. The artifact is a VirtualBox virtual machine image (Ubuntu 22.04 Server, no desktop; 8 CPUs, 16 GB of memory) in which everything is installed. Reviewers log in with SSH (ssh -p 2222 artifact@localhost, password artifact) and run one command, ./run_all.sh; every step is a terminal command. The results are written to one folder per table or figure, with the paper's values next to the reproduced ones and a checklist of the paper's main claims. Download (19 parts of 100 MB), join and check: for i in $(seq -w 0 18); do wget -c -O GeneCS-artifact.ova.part$i "https://zenodo.org/records/23246351/files/GeneCS-artifact.ova.part$i?download=1"; done cat GeneCS-artifact.ova.part* > GeneCS-artifact.ova echo "186fae29c317116f76de0731a822975a6be08c373b45d0b462c82b5bcd163c8f GeneCS-artifact.ova" | sha256sum -c In the VM, in ~/GeneCS-artifact (each run goes on in the background: you can log out of the VM, tail -f run.log shows the progress, Ctrl+C only stops following it; a run that is interrupted continues where it stopped when started again): ./run_all.sh --quick # quick test (~5 min) nohup ./run_all.sh > run.log 2>&1 & # full run as in the paper, Figure 9 with 10^6 shots per point (~3 days) nohup ./run_all.sh --shots 5 > run.log 2>&1 & # shorter: Figure 9 with 10^5 shots per point (~10 h) nohup ./run_all.sh --shots 4 > run.log 2>&1 & # shortest: Figure 9 with 10^4 shots per point (~2.5 h) tail -f run.log # follow the progress GeneCS-artifact.tar.gz holds README.md and the same sources, benchmarks and scripts as the VM. Requirements: an x86-64 computer with VirtualBox 7.1 or later and an SSH client; 8 CPUs (the number can be changed with one command, see the README), 16 GB of memory and 60 GB of disk for the VM. Apple Silicon Macs cannot run the x86-64 image. No network is needed for the experiments. Time (VM with 8 CPUs): quick test ~5 min; full run as in the paper ~3 days (Figure 9 with 10^6 shots per point); shorter full runs with 10^5 or 10^4 shots per point (./run_all.sh --shots 5 or --shots 4): ~10 h or ~2.5 h. The reproduced numbers may differ slightly from the paper's (machine-dependent synthesis times, Monte Carlo logical error rates), but they should match the paper closely.

It gives every step line by line, with copy-paste commands: downloading and starting the VM, running the experiments, where each table and figure is written, and how long each step takes. The summary below is only an overview. The artifact is a VirtualBox virtual machine image (Ubuntu 22.04 Server, no desktop; 8 CPUs, 16 GB of memory) in which everything is installed. Reviewers log in with SSH (ssh -p 2222 artifact@localhost, password artifact) and run one command, ./run_all.sh; every step is a terminal command. The results are written to one folder per table or figure, with the paper's values next to the reproduced ones and a checklist of the paper's main claims. Download (19 parts of 100 MB), join and check: for i in $(seq -w 0 18); do wget -c -O GeneCS-artifact.ova.part$i "https://zenodo.org/records/23246351/files/GeneCS-artifact.ova.part$i?download=1"; done cat GeneCS-artifact.ova.part* > GeneCS-artifact.ova echo "186fae29c317116f76de0731a822975a6be08c373b45d0b462c82b5bcd163c8f GeneCS-artifact.ova" | sha256sum -c In the VM, in ~/GeneCS-artifact (each run goes on in the background: you can log out of the VM, tail -f run.log shows the progress, Ctrl+C only stops following it; a run that is interrupted continues where it stopped when started again): ./run_all.sh --quick # quick test (~5 min) nohup ./run_all.sh > run.log 2>&1 & # full run as in the paper, Figure 9 with 10^6 shots per point (~3 days) nohup ./run_all.sh --shots 5 > run.log 2>&1 & # shorter: Figure 9 with 10^5 shots per point (~10 h) nohup ./run_all.sh --shots 4 > run.log 2>&1 & # shortest: Figure 9 with 10^4 shots per point (~2.5 h) tail -f run.log # follow the progress GeneCS-artifact.tar.gz holds README.md and the same sources, benchmarks and scripts as the VM. Requirements: an x86-64 computer with VirtualBox 7.1 or later and an SSH client; 8 CPUs (the number can be changed with one command, see the README), 16 GB of memory and 60 GB of disk for the VM. Apple Silicon Macs cannot run the x86-64 image. No network is needed for the experiments. Time (VM with 8 CPUs): quick test ~5 min; full run as in the paper ~3 days (Figure 9 with 10^6 shots per point); shorter full runs with 10^5 or 10^4 shots per point (./run_all.sh --shots 5 or --shots 4): ~10 h or ~2.5 h. title: Nerenchi Bot: A robotic system for playing the board game ‘Nerenchi’ against a human opponent
abstract: The Sri Lankan board game Nerenchi, known for its rules and strategic depth, is played by two players, which requires skill and strategy. Nerenchi has two stages: the placing stage to place tokens and the moving stage to move tokens along the lines. The objective is to arrange three tokens in a straight line. Due to technological evolution and the modern world, people cannot experience the actual experience in the physical environment. Although Nerenchi is on the verge of extinction, innovative approaches to updating and conserving these games are necessary to keep them culturally relevant and engaging for modern audiences. This Paper reports the design and development of an intelligent gaming-robot capable of competing against a human, named as ‘Nerenchi Bot’. The proposed main system comprises three sub systems, mainly, the Monitoring system, the Decision-making system and the Robotic system. The Monitoring System automatically determines all the positions of the board and the tokens, using edge detection, grid detection and color detection techniques through OpenCV at 95% of accuracy and generates 24 index position array. The Decision-making system used an algorithm that acts according to game rules, to decide the next movement. The monitoring system and the decision-making system communicate through the position array. According to the index values, the system is capable of deciding the next step according to the principles and game rules. The Robotic system, comprised of a robotic arm, using servo motors, performs actions such as placing, removing, and replacing tokens. These subsystems and the whole system were separately tested with experienced human opponents. More than 100 matches were played with human opponents, and the results were encouraging. This paper also demonstrates the system’s viability by detailing its hardware, computer vision, and decision-making methods.

title: Case Studies and Real-World Deployments of Explainable AI in Cybersecurity
abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed cybersecurity by enabling rapid threat detection, automated response, and large-scale analysis of network data. However, the black-box nature of many machine learning models limits transparency, trust, and regulatory compliance. Explainable AI (XAI) addresses these challenges by providing interpretable explanations that support auditing, decision-making, and model improvement. This chapter reviews the application of XAI in intrusion detection, malware classification, fraud detection, and network anomaly detection. It examines widely used techniques, including SHAP, LIME, attention mechanisms, and rule-based surrogate models, and discusses key deployment challenges such as computational overhead, scalability, adversarial robustness, and regulatory compliance. The chapter provides a practical reference for researchers and cybersecurity professionals developing trustworthy AI-driven security systems.

title: Child-Centric Voice Anonymization in Single and Multi-Speaker Speech via Domain-Adapted SSL Models
abstract: Voice anonymization aims to protect speaker identity while preserving linguistic content and speech usability. However, most anonymization systems are developed on adult speech, leading to degraded performance when applied to child speech. This paper investigates child-centric anonymization by adapting a self-supervised learning (SSL) based anonymization pipeline to the child speech domain. The system is adapted using child speech from the MyST corpus and evaluated under both single-speaker and two-speaker mixture conditions. Experimental results show that child-domain adaptation improves intelligibility and perceptual quality while maintaining strong privacy protection. Extending the approach to multi-speaker further demonstrates that combining target speaker extraction with child-adapted anonymization provides privacy protection while preserving conversational structure. These findings highlight the importance of child-specific adaptation for practical speech anonymization systems

title: High-fidelity spatiotemporal feature extraction for heterogeneous DAS signals
abstract: Disturbance event recognition in Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) systems faces significant multi-scale heterogeneous challenges. Traditional fixed-length sliding windows often lead to morphological truncation or high data redundancy, severely destroying macroscopic topological semantics. This paper proposes a high-fidelity feature extraction framework based on spatiotemporal joint optimization. Universally, multi-channel Pearson cross-correlation spatial fusion suppresses fading dead zones and background noise, while an adaptive hysteresis wrapping mechanism captures the complete lifecycle of heterogeneous events. To ensure fairness, a unified Time-Scale Normalization (TSN) protocol maps features into standard 2D receptive fields. Coupled with the spatial fusion, it effectively decouples the contradiction between scale compression and noise densification. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework overcomes semantic destruction from blind cutting, mitigating the directional misclassification of Clip as Knock from 90.9% down to 62.5%. Compared to traditional 1.0 s windows, the proposed method reduces the system front-end data representation payload by 59% while maintaining an excellent comprehensive recognition rate of 95.62%, offering a high-energy-efficiency edge computing paradigm for computationally constrained DAS terminals.

title: New infinite families of tight sets in Q−(7,q) and related minimal linear codes
abstract: As an important class of finite geometric structures, intriguing sets have attracted extensive research attention. In this paper, we study tight sets, a type of intriguing set, in the polar space Q − ( 7 , q ) . The embedding of Q ( 6 , q ) in Q − ( 7 , q ) yields a ( q 3 + 1 ) -tight set. Since explicit constructions of nontrivial i -tight sets in Q − ( 7 , q ) are relatively rare, we investigate the three orbits O 1 , O 2 , and O 3 of PSL 3 ( q ) on Q − ( 7 , q ) . We prove that, when q is a prime power satisfying q ≡ 2 ( mod 3 ) , these orbits are tight sets with parameters q + 1 , q ( q 2 − 1 ) , and q 3 ( q − 1 ) , respectively. We further prove that O 1 , O 2 , and O 1 ∪ O 2 are nontrivial, thereby obtaining new infinite families of nontrivial tight sets. Additionally, we use the constructed ( q + 1 ) -tight set in Q − ( 7 , q ) to construct a minimal linear code over F q when q ≥ 5 .
